text: dsh-plugin-rtl-text 是面向 DSH Web 和 Desktop GUI 的双向文本排版插件，通过 Cordis 的 webserver/index-inject 扩展点向页面加入样式与脚本，为聊天段落按文本首个强方向字符设置默认方向，并修正英文开头但波斯语占多数或结尾为波斯语的段落。它还让列表、引用和表格容器的标记或列方向跟随内容，隔离混合文字的行内代码，并固定代码块为左到右显示。脚本会在流式内容变化时重新计算方向并清除过期标记；消息文本本身不被改写。适合在网页或桌面聊天界面阅读含阿拉伯语、波斯语和英文混排的回复。通过配置 enabled 可关闭注入；不需要额外配置。

dsh-plugin-rtl-text fixes mixed Persian, Arabic, and English direction in DSH Web and Desktop chat. It injects styles and a script through webserver/index-inject. Text blocks follow their content; code is isolated and code blocks stay left-to-right. Live changes update without rewriting messages.
想让 DSH 聊天里的波斯语和英语混排内容按正确方向显示。
阿拉伯语回复中的英文词和标点总是乱序，怎么修？
让聊天列表项目符号和引用线跟随从右到左的文字。
希望代码行里的波斯语和英文各自保持可读方向。
桌面版聊天怎样正确呈现混合方向的语言？
How can I fix mixed Persian and English text that renders in the wrong order in DSH chat?
Make chat list markers and quote bars follow right-to-left content.
Keep inline code readable when it mixes Arabic or Persian with Latin text.
dsh-plugin-rtl-text 的功能「段落方向修正」：聊天文本块默认按 Unicode 首个强字符确定方向；英文开头但波斯语词较多或以波斯语结束的块会固定为 RTL。 由页面注入脚本自动处理聊天内容。
dsh-plugin-rtl-text 的功能「列表与引用布局」：聊天中的列表、引用和表格容器按内容决定方向，使项目符号、编号、引用线及列顺序随 RTL 内容移动。 由页面注入脚本自动处理聊天内容。
dsh-plugin-rtl-text 的功能「混合代码方向处理」：行内代码、键盘与链接等文本按词数多数方向隔离；代码块固定为 LTR，避免继承 RTL 容器方向。 由页面注入脚本自动处理聊天内容。
dsh-plugin-rtl-text: An observer updates chat text direction.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · dsh-plugin-rtl-text：[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-rtl-text)
[](LICENSE)
[](https://github.com/MojtabaFaraji/dsh-plugin-rtl-text)

A DeepSeek Harness (Cordis) plugin that fixes mixed right-to-left / left-to-right text rendering in chat messages on the Web and Desktop GUI.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · dsh-plugin-rtl-text：When a reply mixes Persian or Arabic with English words, code, or numbers, an LTR page reorders the line: sentences read backwards, punctuation attaches to the wrong side, list numbers and bullets stay on the left edge, and quote bars sit on the wrong side. This plugin gives every chat block a direction computed from its own content — without changing a single character of message text.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · What it fixes：- Persian or Arabic paragraphs with embedded English (`سلام، how are you?`) lay out RTL, with the English runs correct inside them. - English-led Persian sentences (`build سبز + ۴ تست پاس …`) that a first-character heuristic would read as LTR. - Sentences that open Persian but contain many Latin technical tokens (`سطح رندر: تابع واقعی renderIndexInjections …`) — they are never flipped to LTR. - List markers and quote bars: `ol` numbers, `ul` bullets, and `blockquote` bars move to the right together with their content. - Inline code with mixed content (`newest=2026-10-07, age=3 روز`): the span is isolated with its own majority direction, so `=`, `-`, `,`, parentheses, and brackets inside code stop rearranging against the paragraph. - Code blocks keep their structure: `pre` is pinned to LTR with isolation, so an RTL context can never scramble code — Persian comments inside render as RTL runs. - File-labeled Persian bullets (`README.md: دو بخش جدید …`): the Latin label opens and even outweighs the Persian letters, but the sentence closes Persian — the last-strong rule keeps the list RTL with its bullets on the right. - Digit-led

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · What it does not change：- **Message text.** The durable session log, model history, and CLI output stay byte-identical; the plugin only touches presentation.
- **Other profiles.** Headless and TUI profiles have no GUI to style — the injected rows are never collected there and the plugin is a harmless no-op.
- **Code block content.** `pre` keeps its authored LTR order (it is pinned, never rewritten) — only its `direction` context is fixed.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Installation：The plugin is installed as a **bundle layer** into a profile — this is what actually mounts it:

```bash
dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · from the npm registry：pnpm dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-plugin-rtl-text

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · from a local checkout (no registry needed)：pnpm dsh plugin --profile <name> add <path-to-this-package>
```

You can also use the GUI **Add plugin** button with the package name. A plain `pnpm add` only copies files into the profile's `node_modules`; it does not append the bundle layer, so the plugin would never mount — prefer the commands above.

Peer dependency: `@deepseek-ai/cordis` (published on npm, and already present in every Harness installation).

text: dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · How it works：The Web markdown renderer deliberately keeps raw HTML inert — no HTML parser enters its pipeline — so a display fix cannot travel inside message text. Instead, the plugin uses the Harness index-injection extension point (`webserver/index-inject`, the same event `ui-theme` uses): on every page load the webserver collects injection rows and renders them into `index.html`, and this plugin appends two rows.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · The `style` row：The no-JavaScript default: each block takes its direction from its first strong character (`unicode-bidi: plaintext`), scoped to chat rows through their stable `data-chat-*` attributes:

```css
:where([data-chat-group-key],[data-chat-flow-key]) :is(p,li,h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6,blockquote,dd,dt,td,th,figcaption){unicode-bidi:plaintext}
```

Sentences that open in their dominant language resolve correctly with no script at all.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · The `script` row: Latin-led Persian sentences：First-strong alone reads `build سبز + ۴ تست پاس` as LTR because it opens with English. When a text block opens LTR yet RTL words (any word holding a Hebrew/Arabic character, including Arabic punctuation and diacritics) outnumber Latin/Greek/Cyrillic words, the script pins `dir="rtl"` — the majority counts words, not characters, because English phrases inside Persian prose are character-dense (`README.md: بند جدید در «What it fixes» …` ties the character count 60/60 yet is Persian by words, 18 to 9) with an inline `unicode-bidi: isolate` so the explicit direction wins over the stylesheet. Sentences that open Persian are never pinned — technical Latin tokens such as `renderIndexInjections` must not flip `سطح رندر: تابع واقعی …` to LTR, so first-strong keeps them RTL. A sentence that opens with a Latin label yet closes Persian (`README.md: دو بخش جدید …`) is authored Persian: blocks and lists whose last strong character is Persian are pinned RTL too. Arabic-Indic and Persian digits (`۰`–`۹`) are numbers, not strong characters — the RTL ranges exclude them, so a `۱.`-led item is read exactly as `unicode-bidi: pl

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Container direction: list numbers, bullets, quote bars：Markers follow the container's own `direction` property, which `unicode-bidi: plaintext` on the inner text cannot change — on an LTR page they would stay on the left edge. For chat-scoped `ul`, `ol`, `blockquote`, and `table` the script applies the full rule (RTL when the text opens Persian, closes Persian, or holds an RTL majority) and pins an inline `direction: rtl`, so a list opening `1. اولین مورد …` keeps its numbers on the right with the text. English lists stay left. Tables join the same rule for their **column order** (a `مرحله / نتیجه` table keeps its first column on the right), while every cell keeps `unicode-bidi: plaintext` for its content — a Latin-heavy result cell stays LTR inside the RTL table.
section: Container direction: list numbers, bullets, quote bars

text: dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Inline code, links, and code blocks：`=`, `-`, `,`, `(`, `)` and `[` are neutral characters: inside a paragraph they take their direction from the surrounding text, which is exactly why `newest=2026-10-07, age=3 روز` scrambled in RTL context. Chat-scoped `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `var`, and `a` therefore take their **own majority direction** (ties fall back to first-strong) with an inline `unicode-bidi: isolate` — each becomes one coherent island whose symbols stay where they were written, and nested Persian inside Latin-majority code still renders RTL. Code blocks (`pre` and `pre code`) are pinned to `dir="ltr"` so code structure never inherits an RTL direction from a pinned ancestor. Symbols in plain text outside any element follow the paragraph direction the plugin computes; if one still looks wrong, open an issue with the exact sentence.
section: Inline code, links, and code blocks

text:
dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Inline code, links, and code blocks：A `MutationObserver` reapplies every decision as streaming text grows, removes a stale pin when the text no longer qualifies, and watches text and child mutations only — attribute writes never loop.

**What is never touched:** message text itself. The durable session log, model history, and CLI output stay byte-identical, and messages already in history are fixed too because the mechanism is presentation-only.
section: Inline code, links, and code blocks

text:
dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Compatibility：- Requires a DeepSeek Harness release that exposes `webserver/index-inject` and chat rows carrying `data-chat-group-key` / `data-chat-flow-key` — current releases do.
- Both extension points are pre-stable public APIs. When upgrading the Harness across versions, rerun `pnpm run test` and check that chat rows still carry those attributes; a Harness-side rename would need a matching selector update here.
- Applies to the Web GUI and the Desktop GUI (the same document). Headless and TUI profiles are unaffected.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `enabled` | `true` | Set `false` to keep the plugin mounted without contributing rows. |

Override it in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` with an id-targeted patch:

```yaml
- id: rtl-text
  config:
    enabled: false
```

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Where is cordis.yml?：1. **`<profile>/cordis.yml`** — the profile's root entry list. It stays empty; the file header says to edit `cordis.patch.yml` instead.
2. **`<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`** — the profile's own patch layer (id-targeted overrides and `disabled` flags), applied *above* every bundle layer.
3. **`cordis.patch.yml` inside this package** — this plugin's bundle layer, shipped with the package and referenced by `dsh.bundle.patch`. The loader reads it when the package is installed as a bundle; you do not edit it.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | What to do |
|---------|-----------|
| Installed and reloaded, but nothing changed | Remount first (plugin page: off → on, or restart the host), *then* reload. Rows are collected from the live mounted plugin at page load. |
| One sentence still has the wrong direction | Heuristic limit: a nearly balanced bilingual sentence falls back to its first strong character. [Open an issue](https://github.com/MojtabaFaraji/dsh-plugin-rtl-text/issues) with the exact sentence. |
| List numbers or bullets still on the left | Confirm the reload followed the remount. If your Harness version renamed the chat row attributes, the selector needs a matching update (see [Compatibility](#compatibility)). |
| You want it off | Set `enabled: false` as shown in [Configuration](#configuration). |

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Security and privacy：- The plugin contributes two static rows — one CSS block and one inline script — built from constants inside the package. No message content is embedded, no network requests are made, and nothing is stored.
- The script reads `textContent` of chat blocks and writes `dir`/inline style on them; a `MutationObserver` only watches for new content. Nothing leaves the page.
- Because message text is never rewritten, transcripts and model history stay byte-identical.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Example：- Reply `سلام، how are you?`: before, the paragraph follows the page direction and runs and punctuation reappear in the wrong order; after, the direction comes from `سلام` — a full RTL line with `how are you` rendered LTR inside it.
- A list item starting `build سبز + ۴ تست پاس …`: first-strong reads the opening `build` as LTR and breaks the Persian sentence; the script counts the Persian letters as the majority and pins `dir="rtl"` for the whole block.
- `سطح رندر: تابع واقعی renderIndexInjections → style در <head> …`: first-strong already reads the opening `سطح` as RTL, so the script stays out of it — the Latin technical tokens outnumber the Persian letters, but a majority override here would wrongly flip the sentence to LTR.
- A list or quote starting with a number (`1. اولین مورد …`) or a bullet: the marker follows the container's direction, not the text's — the script pins the `ul`/`ol`/`blockquote` itself with `dir="rtl"` and an inline `direction: rtl`, so the numbers and bullets move to the right with their items.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Testing：The suite covers both injection rows (preserving other rows, never emitting `</script`), the pinning rules against both reported failure directions (English-led Persian forced RTL; Persian-led Latin-heavy left to first-strong), container pinning for lists and quotes (numbers, bullets, quote bars); inline-code isolation against the reported `newest=2026-10-07, age=3 روز` case; LTR code-block pinning; last-strong pinning for file-labeled Persian bullets; stale-pin removal, the `enabled: false` configuration, listener unwind on `fiber.dispose()`, and two-rows-per-collection semantics.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Building from source：```bash
pnpm run build   # tsdown → lib/index.js + lib/index.d.ts
```

Run this inside the package directory only. The DeepSeek Harness repository root has its own monorepo `tsdown.config.ts` which expects `tsc`-emitted `lib/types/{index,invariant,startup}.js` entries; building from the repository root picks up that config instead of the package-local one and fails.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Building from source：The package has no runtime dependencies, so a `pnpm install` of this package alone is not required. Building and testing need `tsdown` and `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, which resolve from an adjacent DeepSeek Harness checkout — this is where development happens.

dsh-plugin-rtl-text README · Publishing a release：1. Green checks: `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run test` (from a checkout inside the Harness tree, as above).
2. Inspect the tarball: `npm pack --dry-run` — expect `lib/index.js`, `lib/index.d.ts`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `LICENSE`.
3. Bump `version` and add an entry to [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).
4. `npm login` then `npm publish` — `prepublishOnly` rebuilds `lib/` automatically.
5. Push to GitHub ([MojtabaFaraji/dsh-plugin-rtl-text](https://github.com/MojtabaFaraji/dsh-plugin-rtl-text)): the repository commits `lib/` on purpose so a plain clone works without the Harness toolchain; `.gitignore` excludes only `node_modules/`, local npm caches, tarballs, and logs.
